[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Mastering Layout Systems in NativeScript: Stack, Grid, Flexbox, and Absolute"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Building cross-platform mobile applications requires a robust understanding of layout systems. NativeScript provides a powerful set of layout containers that help you organize UI components efficiently across different screen sizes and orientations. In this tutorial, we will explore the four primary NativeScript layouts: StackLayout, GridLayout, FlexboxLayout, and AbsoluteLayout."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"1. StackLayout: Linear Arrangement"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"The StackLayout arranges items in a single line, either vertically or horizontally. By default, the orientation is vertical. It is commonly used for form fields, lists of simple elements, or sequential UI flows."},{"order":5,"type":"code","text":"<StackLayout orientation="vertical" padding="20">
    <Label text="First Item" class="title" />
    <Label text="Second Item" class="body" />
    <Button text="Click Me" />
</StackLayout>"},{"order":6,"type":"subheading","text":"2. GridLayout: Complex Matrix Structures"},{"order":7,"type":"paragraph","text":"The GridLayout is arguably the most versatile layout container in NativeScript. It lets you define rows and columns using absolute, auto, and star (*) sizing. You can precisely place elements inside specific cells using row and col properties."},{"order":8,"type":"code","text":"<GridLayout rows="auto, *, 50" columns="*, *" padding="10">
    <Label row="0" col="0" colSpan="2" text="Header Span" />
    <Button row="1" col="0" text="Left Action" />
    <Button row="1" col="1" text="Right Action" />
    <Label row="2" col="0" colSpan="2" text="Footer" />
</GridLayout>"},{"order":9,"type":"subheading","text":"3. FlexboxLayout: Responsive Flexibility"},{"order":10,"type":"paragraph","text":"Modeled after the CSS Flexbox model, the FlexboxLayout gives you powerful control over alignment, direction, and wrapping of child elements. It is ideal for dynamic interfaces where items need to wrap or stretch depending on screen dimensions."},{"order":11,"type":"code","text":"<FlexboxLayout flexDirection="row" justifyContent="space-around" alignItems="center">
    <Button text="Item 1" />
    <Button text="Item 2" />
    <Button text="Item 3" />
</FlexboxLayout>"},{"order":12,"type":"subheading","text":"4. AbsoluteLayout: Exact Coordinate Positioning"},{"order":13,"type":"paragraph","text":"The AbsoluteLayout positions its children using explicit absolute coordinates (left and top) along with width and height. While less responsive than other layouts, it is indispensable for custom graphics, overlays, badges, and games."},{"order":14,"type":"code","text":"<AbsoluteLayout width="300" height="300">
    <Label text="Base Layer" left="0" top="0" width="300" height="300" backgroundColor="lightgray" />
    <Button text="Overlay Button" left="50" top="100" width="200" height="50" />
</AbsoluteLayout>"},{"order":15,"type":"subheading","text":"Best Practices for Choosing a Layout"},{"order":16,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Use StackLayout for simple, sequential lists of items where complexity is low."},{"order":17,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Use GridLayout for forms, dashboards, and structured UI components that require precise grid alignments."},{"order":18,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Use FlexboxLayout when building toolbars, wrap-around tag lists, or dynamically shifting responsive UIs."},{"order":19,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Reserve AbsoluteLayout exclusively for floating UI elements, animations, or precise overlapping components."},{"order":20,"type":"paragraph","text":"By combining these native layout containers effectively, you can build fluid, high-performance cross-platform applications with NativeScript that adapt seamlessly to any device resolution."}]
